summary: Iteration 6: Verified /login deep-link fix and vehicle-marker halo removal. Found and fixed a REMAINING /login regression: fetchMe's 401 catch called logout() on initial anonymous mount, which reset activeTab back to 'home' and pushState to '/'. Wrapped logout() call to only fire when there was an existing token/user. After the fix: /login deep-link renders the login form and URL stays /login. Header 'Log In' click flips URL to /login. All 3 seed accounts login and route correctly. Backend pytest: 12/12 green. Vehicle-marker source in MapView.jsx confirmed correct (plain 20px blue dot, no car emoji, no wide halo). Live map on active ride currently shows only pickup(green)+destination(red) markers because captain_location is null on the tested ride; vehicle marker code verified via source inspection.
action_items: None – critical /login deep-link bug fixed by testing agent (fetchMe catch guarded). Please retest end-to-end once and confirm.
Optional: verify vehicle marker visually by triggering captain_location broadcast on an active ride (source code already correct).
critical_code_review_comments: App.js is 1923 lines – strongly recommend splitting (Auth, Booking, Delivery, Rentals, Driver, Admin views) into separate modules. File-size lint threshold >700 lines is breached.

fetchMe previously called logout() on any /auth/me failure including initial anonymous load — this reset routing state. Fixed by gating on (token || user). Consider a dedicated 'session bootstrap' effect that runs once and doesn't disturb routing.
The two /login-sync useEffects rely on window.history manipulation. Consider migrating to react-router to avoid re-inventing this and prevent similar regressions.
Multiple duplicated fetch patterns (fetchRides/fetchRentals/fetchDeliveries) — extract a useAuthedFetch hook.
updated_files: /app/frontend/src/App.js (fetchMe catch now guards logout on anonymous initial load)
context_for_next_testing_agent: The /login deep-link fix required TWO changes: (a) lazy useState init of activeTab from window.location.pathname, (b) didMountRef guard, AND (c) the missing piece I added — fetchMe's catch must NOT call logout() on initial anonymous mount since logout() setActiveTab('home') overrides the lazy 'login' init. If regressions recur, check fetchMe first.
rca of the issue: RCA: On direct navigation to /login while logged out: activeTab lazy-inits to 'login'. On mount, useEffect([token]) fires fetchMe(). Backend returns 401 (no cookie). The catch called logout() which does setActiveTab('home'). Then the /login-sync effect (didMountRef now true after first run) sees activeTab!='login' and path='/login', pushes state to '/'. Net effect: URL flips to / and homepage renders. Fix: only call logout() from fetchMe catch when (token || user) is truthy, so anonymous initial load is a no-op.
